text: Teke-Kukuya is a stable indigenous language of Congo. It belongs to the Niger-Congo language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.

text: In all, there are more than sixty languages spoken in Congo. Languages with more than ten thousand speakers include Akwa, Bobangi, Bomwali, French, Kituba (a Kongo-based creole), Kunyi, Laari, Likuba, Likwala, Mbere, Mboko, Mbosi, Nbaka Ma'bo, Ngugwel, Njebi, Ombamba, Suundi, Teke-Ebbo, Teke-Ibali, Teke-Kukuyu, Teke-Nzikou, Teke-Tege, Teke-Tsaayi, Teke-Tyee, Tsaangi, Yay, and Yombe. All of these except for French fall within the Niger-Congo language classification, and all are considered living languages.
